## Two costumes you have to earn

v1.5.15 was all hill. This one is Squachy's wardrobe, a battery menu, and four settings rows that stop and ask before they do something you cannot take back.

Both new outfits are earned on the background they belong to, not by grinding a detection count. Neither is mentioned anywhere on the device.

### VOID EYE

On **STARFIELD**, catch two eyes in a row. His head becomes one.

Stars drift inside the sphere and the iris tracks, both read from tables baked into flash rather than worked out every frame — forty-six star directions in sixty-fourths, a sixty-four entry square-root ramp, eight iris spokes. It costs program space instead of the memory Squachy needs for everything else he is doing.

The first version of it was **completely invisible on the real panel**. This display gives blue four levels where red and green get eight, so everything below about a quarter brightness rounds down to nothing: a near-black sclera and a deep navy fur both came out as flat black, and the whole costume rendered as a Squachy-shaped hole. Every colour in it is now picked off that four-step ramp on purpose, and the outline is a violet rim rather than a darker black that was never going to survive.

While you are on that screen: **the werewolf now takes five taps on the moon, not ten.** Ten was too long a hold for something nobody is told about.

### SNOW PARKA

On **SNOWFALL**, knock five times on the lodge.

His own face and his own shades, inside a hood pulled tight, with no mouth. The hood is the part that took the work. There is no clipping when drawing into the frame buffer, so a hood that is genuinely *in front* of him cannot be had by drawing things in the right order — his head is drawn full size underneath and his ears and jaw reach past the opening either way. The hood is refilled row by row over the top of him instead, which paints those out.

The black ring around his face is filled by that same pass rather than drawn as an outline afterwards. When it was an outline you got **orange flecks scattered through the brown around his face**: the fill worked out its edge one way and the outline stepped its own another way, and wherever the curve runs flat the two landed a pixel apart and hood orange showed through the gap between them. One number per row makes that impossible.

His boots, mittens and sleeves also had to learn where his limbs actually are rather than where they rest. More on that below.

### POWER SAVER

A new screen in Settings. Screen timeout, backlight dim, a frame cap when idle, the processor clock, and what a wake tap does — each one switched on and adjusted on its own, each remembered across a reboot.

The display's own clock is deliberately **not** one of them. That one is fixed when the firmware is built, and the flasher already offers it as a choice at install time where undoing it is a reflash rather than something you have to find in a menu on a display that may be the thing that broke.

### Settings that ask first

Four rows now put a panel up before they act: **CALIBRATE TOUCH**, **RESET STATS**, **BORING MODE** and **REPLAY INTRO**.

The rule for earning one is that tapping the row a second time does not put things back. Calibration overwrites the calibration you are using before it knows the new one is any good. Reset zeroes the lifetime count that most of the outfits are gated on, so **it takes them away again** — the panel says so, because nothing else on the screen did. And boring mode hides every Squachy row, which is exactly how it manages to be hard to undo: the first thing it takes away is the OUTFIT row. That panel names OUTFIT and tells you the same row turns it back off.

Boring mode only asks on the way in. Turning it off restores everything it hid, and asking there would just be friction on the fix.

The title-bar long-press keeps no panel at all. It is the way back in when touch is already too far out to land on a button, which is precisely when a button between you and a working screen is the last thing you want.

### The tanooki tail is a tail now

It was a row of stacked circles, which read as a balloon animal. It is a curve with the width falling away late, a travelling S-shaped wiggle running down it, and a fur texture that is a **wobble in its own thickness** rather than extra circles hung off the sides — those stuck out past the outline and read as debris rather than fur.

**His mouth works in that costume again.** The snout was painted on last, after the mood had already drawn a mouth, so it stamped one fixed expression over every single thing he does.

### Two more things

**Somebody else walks past the toasters.** A little guy crosses the bottom of the **After Dark** background once every five minutes, on the same line Mowin' Man uses. The two of them are interlocked, so whichever is already out there keeps the line and the other comes back for it in a few seconds rather than the pair of them walking through each other.

**Fireflies over the meadow**, the yeti's eating fixed, and the diagnostics screen now tells you how long the background has been running.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: VOID EYE, earned by catching two eyes in a row on STARFIELD
- **Added**: SNOW PARKA, earned by knocking five times on the lodge on SNOWFALL
- **Added**: POWER SAVER, with screen timeout, dim, idle frame cap, processor clock and wake behaviour
- **Added**: confirmation panels on CALIBRATE TOUCH, RESET STATS, BORING MODE and REPLAY INTRO
- **Added**: a little guy walks the After Dark line every five minutes
- **Added**: fireflies over the meadow
- **Added**: the diagnostics screen shows how long the background has run
- **Changed**: the werewolf takes five taps on the moon instead of ten
- **Changed**: the tanooki tail is a tapered curve with a travelling wiggle instead of stacked circles
- **Fixed**: the tanooki snout painted one fixed mouth over every mood
- **Fixed**: the parka's boots stayed put while his feet walked out from under them
- **Fixed**: his mitten floated beside his head when he waved, with nothing joining it to the arm
- **Fixed**: orange flecks in the brown around the parka's face
- **Fixed**: his legs turned a different colour from his coat during the rare rainbow shimmer
- **Fixed**: shoulder outlines showed through the hood
- **Fixed**: Mowin' Man and the little guy could walk the same line at the same time
